<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

Allow sweep plot filters to match values containing commas when the entire value is quoted.

Related to #60510, but separate in scope: that PR handles comparison-operator characters inside a single filter value; this change handles separators between filter expressions and leaves operator selection unchanged.

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- Preserve commas inside matching single- or double-quoted filter values while retaining ordinary comma-separated filters.
- Start quoting only at the initial comparison's value boundary, preserving literal quotes later in an unquoted target.
- Reject unterminated quoted values with an explicit error.
- Preserve literal apostrophes and backslashes in unquoted values; update CLI help and rendered documentation.

## Validation

<!-- Show evidence that the claims are met by this change, and steps to reproduce validations. -->

Validated on Windows x86_64 with Python 3.12.15, CPU-only Torch 2.14.0, NumPy 2.2.6, pandas 2.2.3, and the repository-pinned Ruff 0.14.0 / mypy 1.20.2.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Original PR test revision with production code at `e9acf48614` | 6 failed, 36 passed |
| Original PR suite before the review follow-up | 42 passed, including real CLI filtering |
| New boundary regressions against reviewed head `a0ada888` | 7 failed, 43 passed |
| Current owning suite after the boundary fix | 50 passed, including three additional real CLI cases |
| Python 3.11 type-check target | Passed, 2 source files |
| Repository hooks | Python, docs, typos, oldest-Python mypy, SPDX, import checks, and Buildkite test tethering passed |
| Full hook invocation | Exit 1 only because the unrelated Docker graph hook requires absolute `/bin/bash` on Windows |
| Same Docker graph script invoked with Git Bash | Passed with the actual staged filenames; Dockerfile is unchanged |
| Commit-time hooks | All other checks passed; only the unsupported Docker launcher was skipped after its script passed directly |

Run from this branch with the isolated uv environment active:

```powershell
# Reviewed source a0ada888 plus new cases: 7 failed, 43 passed.
# Current source after the review fix: 50 passed.
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests\benchmarks tests\benchmarks\test_plot_filters.py -q

# Passed.
uv run --active --no-project mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent vllm\benchmarks\sweep\plot.py tests\benchmarks\test_plot_filters.py

# Relevant checks passed; the full invocation has the Windows launcher limitation above.
$env:PYTHONUTF8 = "1"
uv run --active --no-project pre-commit run

# Passed using the installed Git Bash.
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.\tools\pre_commit\update-dockerfile-graph.sh').Path @(git --no-pager diff --cached --name-only)
```

Git Bash's `bin` and `usr\bin` directories were on `PATH` for repository hooks. Source-only imports emit the expected warning about missing generated version metadata. No model, serving, GPU, or performance evaluation was run; those execution paths are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Review regression: relevant before/after output</summary>

With the new regressions and production code from reviewed head `a0ada888`:

```text
ValueError: Unterminated quoted value in plot filter "label==build=='one"
7 failed, 43 passed, 1 warning in 23.82s
```

After the boundary fix, using the same pytest command:

```text
50 passed, 1 warning in 9.34s
```

</details>

## Details

<!-- Explain motivation, design decisions, root cause, tradeoffs, and limitations concisely. Link or collapse lengthy supporting material. -->

The previous unconditional comma split turned `_benchmark_name=="fp8,tp2"` into two invalid expressions. The parser now tracks matching quotes around a value and recognizes only unquoted commas as separators.

The implementation deliberately avoids shell tokenization so existing apostrophes and Windows-style backslashes remain literal. Tests assert actual DataFrame selection, existing numeric/boolean behavior, malformed-input errors, and the real CLI's handling of a quoted value combined with another condition. No dependencies are added.

The [follow-up commit](https://github.com/singh4jitendra/vllm/commit/66469328bb4432ea88f5f735f375d208766fea7f) addresses [BlueRaddish's review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63469#pullrequestreview-5642352514): comparison-like text inside an unquoted target must not open quoting again. The scanner now remembers the first comparison's value boundary in each expression and only starts quoting while that value prefix is empty or whitespace. The boundary resets at an unquoted comma. Coverage includes the reported literal targets, a whitespace variant, three real CLI regressions, and a quoted value following an earlier expression.

Duplicate checks on October 24 searched open PRs for quoted commas, sweep quoting, and `PlotFilters`, and inspected the current patch of #60510. That patch changes `PlotFilterBase` operator selection; it leaves the comma splitting addressed here unchanged.

Before the original PR was opened, the human submitter confirmed reviewing the original patch and running its documented tests, and explicitly authorized the personal GitHub noreply DCO sign-off and required AI attribution. The author subsequently requested this review fix; the follow-up commit and its validation evidence are recorded above.

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

The quote scanner also starts quoting **inside an already-started unquoted target**, which regresses preservation of literal quotes in unquoted values. At `a0ada888b53b38403fb294c2e2e8234e8dfe6f39`:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["build=='one", "other"]})
PlotFilters.parse_str("label==build=='one").apply(df)
# ValueError: Unterminated quoted value in plot filter ...
```

The upstream merge parent `66bf931544202f159cf83c66a812826b7d5c84fb` selects `build=='one` correctly. The `endswith(tuple(PLOT_FILTERS))` condition recognizes the **second** `==` as a value boundary. The same regression affects `build!="one` and `version>='one`; it is distinct from #60510 because the first `==` already selects the intended operator and the target does not begin with an operator.

Please start outer quoting only at the initial comparison's value boundary, leaving later quotes in an unquoted value literal, and add a regression in `test_plot_filters.py`.

Verified through the real CPU/empty-target installation: **10 parent consumers pass; this head has 7 matching failures / 3 controls**, including three real CLI-to-`main()` filtering cases. The existing **42 owning tests pass**, so they currently miss this regression. A local diagnostic boundary check passes all **52 cases**; it was then removed and exact source bytes restored. [Actual job and logs](https://github.com/BlueRaddish/agent-framework/actions/runs/40177892695/job/121122443779). No source, sign-off or PR metadata change; no model/server/GPU or full plotting-render evaluation. AI-assisted review with Codex.

files.patch:
@@ -210,6 +210,14 @@ vllm bench sweep startup \
 
 Control the variables to plot via `--var-x` and `--var-y`, optionally applying `--filter-by` and `--bin-by` to the values. The plot is organized according to `--fig-by`, `--row-by`, `--col-by`, and `--curve-by`.
 
+Wrap an entire filter value in single or double quotes if it contains commas. Only commas outside quoted values separate filters. Unterminated quoted values are rejected.
+Only a quote at the start of the value, after the first comparison operator and optional whitespace, opens a quoted value. Quotes later in an unquoted value, such as `build=='one`, remain literal.
+
+```bash
+vllm bench sweep plot benchmarks/results/demo \
+    --filter-by '_benchmark_name=="fp8,tp2",max_concurrency>=8'
+```
+
 Example commands for visualizing [Workload Explorer](#workload-explorer) results:
 
 ```bash

@@ -1,5 +1,8 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
 import pandas as pd
 import pytest
 
@@ -13,7 +16,10 @@
     PlotLessThan,
     PlotLessThanOrEqualTo,
     PlotNotEqualTo,
+    SweepPlotArgs,
+    main,
 )
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
 
 
 class TestPlotFilters:
@@ -226,6 +232,86 @@ def test_parse_multiple_filters(self):
         assert isinstance(filters[0], PlotGreaterThan)
         assert isinstance(filters[1], PlotLessThanOrEqualTo)
 
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "expression,target",
+        [
+            ('label=="fp8,tp2",request_rate<2', "fp8,tp2"),
+            ("label=='fp8,tp2',request_rate<2", "fp8,tp2"),
+            ('label=="O\'Brien,tp2",request_rate<2', "O'Brien,tp2"),
+            ("request_rate<2,label=='fp8,tp2'", "fp8,tp2"),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_quoted_commas_do_not_split_filter_values(self, expression, target):
+        df = pd.DataFrame({"label": [target, "other"], "request_rate": [1, 1]})
+
+        result = PlotFilters.parse_str(expression).apply(df)
+
+        assert result["label"].tolist() == [target]
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "target",
+        [
+            "O'Brien",
+            r"C:\models\example",
+            "build=='one",
+            'build!="one',
+            "version>='one",
+            "build== 'one",
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_unquoted_values_keep_literal_quotes_and_backslashes(self, target):
+        df = pd.DataFrame({"label": [target, "other"]})
+
+        result = PlotFilters.parse_str(f"label=={target}").apply(df)
+
+        assert result["label"].tolist() == [target]
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("expression", ['label=="fp8,tp2', "label=='fp8,tp2"])
+    def test_unterminated_quoted_values_are_rejected(self, expression):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Unterminated quoted value"):
+            PlotFilters.parse_str(expression)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "target,other,expression",
+        [
+            ("fp8,tp2", "fp8", '_benchmark_name=="fp8,tp2",request_rate>1'),
+            ("build=='one", "other", "_benchmark_name==build=='one,request_rate>1"),
+            ('build!="one', "other", '_benchmark_name==build!="one,request_rate>1'),
+            ("version>='one", "other", "_benchmark_name==version>='one,request_rate>1"),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_cli_applies_quoted_and_unquoted_value_filters(
+        self,
+        tmp_path: Path,
+        capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
+        target,
+        other,
+        expression,
+    ):
+        records = [
+            {
+                "_benchmark_name": name,
+                "request_rate": rate,
+                "total_token_throughput": 100,
+                "median_ttft_ms": 10,
+            }
+            for name, rate in [(target, 1), (other, 2)]
+        ]
+        (tmp_path / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(records), encoding="utf-8")
+        parser = SweepPlotArgs.add_cli_args(FlexibleArgumentParser())
+        args = parser.parse_args(
+            [
+                str(tmp_path),
+                "--filter-by",
+                expression,
+            ]
+        )
+
+        main(args)
+
+        assert "No data to plot." in capsys.readouterr().out
+        assert not list(tmp_path.glob("*.png"))
+
     def test_parse_empty_filter(self):
         """Test parsing empty filter string."""
         filters = PlotFilters.parse_str("")

@@ -127,7 +127,31 @@ def parse_str(cls, s: str):
         if not s:
             return cls()
 
-        return cls(PlotFilterBase.parse_str(e) for e in s.split(","))
+        expressions = []
+        quote: str | None = None
+        value_start: int | None = None
+        start = 0
+        for index, char in enumerate(s):
+            if quote is not None:
+                if char == quote:
+                    quote = None
+            elif char == ",":
+                expressions.append(s[start:index])
+                start = index + 1
+                value_start = None
+            elif value_start is None:
+                for op_key in PLOT_FILTERS:
+                    if s.startswith(op_key, index):
+                        value_start = index + len(op_key)
+                        break
+            elif char in ("'", '"') and not s[value_start:index].strip():
+                quote = char
+
+        if quote is not None:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unterminated quoted value in plot filter {s!r}")
+
+        expressions.append(s[start:])
+        return cls(PlotFilterBase.parse_str(e) for e in expressions)
 
     def apply(self, df: "pd.DataFrame") -> "pd.DataFrame":
         for item in self:
@@ -602,6 +626,7 @@ def add_cli_args(cls, parser: FlexibleArgumentParser) -> FlexibleArgumentParser:
             default="",
             help="A comma-separated list of statements indicating values to filter by. "
             "This is useful to remove outliers. "
+            "Quote values containing commas. "
             "Example: `max_concurrency<1000,max_num_batched_tokens<=4096` means "
             "plot only the points where `max_concurrency` is less than 1000 and "
             "`max_num_batched_tokens` is no greater than 4096.",
